Carbohydrates and Fiber
Average carbohydrate intakes in Western populations are close to the recommendation of 50% energy. The main sources in the
adolescent diet are breakfast cereals, bread, savory snacks, vegetables and potatoes. Fiber intakes, expressed as nonstarch polysac-
charide (NSP), are 10–13 g per day in the UK, which is approximately 70% of the adult guideline. Vegetables, potatoes, and savory
snacks together contribute 40% of NSP. Interestingly studies have not always found consistent relationships between ﬁber intakes
and bowel movements in young people. Sugar intakes peak in adolescence before declining to adult levels and are higher in boys
